is_anopheles.evidence: The study evaluates the efficacy of treated blankets against Anopheles gambiae sensu stricto (Abstract, Page 3) and mentions Anopheles arabiensis as the dominant local vector (Methods, Page 10).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper mentions the Vgsc L1014S (L995S) mutation: 'The Muleba-Kis strain... is resistant to permethrin with fixed L1014S kdr frequency' (Methods, Page 10).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper only states that the L1014S mutation is 'fixed' in the Muleba-Kis laboratory colony. It does not provide genotype counts or frequencies for any field-collected populations, nor does it provide the number of mosquitoes genotyped to determine this 'fixed' status in the current study.

african_field_population.evidence: The mosquitoes used for all bioassays and the experimental hut trial were laboratory-reared strains: Kisumu (susceptible) and Muleba-Kis (resistant). Muleba-Kis is described as having been 'colonized for more than 8 years' (Methods, Page 10). No field-collected mosquitoes were genotyped.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study evaluating the efficacy of permethrin-PBO treated blankets.

sub_country_location.evidence: The experimental hut study was conducted at Mabogini village (S03˚22.764’ E03˚720.793’) in north-eastern Tanzania (Methods, Page 10).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The experimental hut trial was conducted from June to July 2021 (Methods, Page 14).

duplicate_risk.evidence: This is a routine evaluation of a new vector control tool (treated blankets) using standard experimental hut protocols.

supplement.evidence: There is no indication that genotype data for field populations is contained in supplementary files; the study design focused on laboratory strains.

assessment.summary: The study evaluates the efficacy of permethrin-PBO treated blankets against laboratory-reared Anopheles gambiae (Kisumu and Muleba-Kis strains) using WHO cylinder bioassays, tunnel tests, and experimental hut trials in Tanzania. While the paper notes that the Muleba-Kis colony has a fixed L1014S kdr mutation, it does not report any genotype data for field-collected mosquitoes.
exclusion_reasons: The study only reports genotype information for laboratory-reared mosquito colonies (Muleba-Kis), which have been colonized for over 8 years. No genotype data for field-collected mosquitoes are provided.
